description: Versioned historical backend changes used as reproducible impact-localization and provider-comparison tasks. Gold paths are verified against each target commit before scoring.

tasks.requirement: Allow an owner to associate an already-persisted pet without adding duplicates, enforce a maximum pet-name length of 30 characters while retaining required-field validation, and add regression tests.
Normalize surrounding whitespace in owner last-name search and cover the behavior in the controller test.
Enforce unique pet names per owner across supported databases and cover controller, service, and concurrency behavior.
Require new visit dates to be strictly in the future, reject today or earlier with a localized validation message, default new visits and the form minimum to tomorrow, and add controller coverage.
Prevent binding direct and nested identifier fields for owners, pets, and visits while preserving existing mutable-field binding and pet validation.

Fix pet update so changes to an existing pet name, birth date, and type are persisted on that pet instead of adding another pet, while preserving the fallback for a pet not yet associated with its owner.
Separate MySQL user creation from privilege grants in the bootstrap script, preserving the existing database, account, and grant settings with MySQL 8-compatible syntax.

Rotate a session refresh hash only when both its ID and current hash match, through the session abstraction and relational/document persistence. Use this conditional update during refresh authentication and reject an absent or stale session without issuing tokens.
Return the domain file value after saving a relational file entity, and make the response interceptor emit resolved data rather than a nested Promise when resolving file values.
Expose an optional global language request header in Swagger, using APP_HEADER_LANGUAGE when configured and x-custom-lang otherwise, with an English language example.
Return the post-update document, rather than its old state, from user/session persistence and both document-only and all-database repository generators, retaining null behavior for absent documents.

Allow an authenticated user to request an email change, normalize and validate it, reject another account's email, and send localized confirmation mail. Preserve the current email until a valid confirmation token is redeemed, activate the user on confirmation, retain password-change checks, and add end-to-end coverage.
Fix user email updates incorrectly rejecting an unused email: accept an email with no matching account or with the same user ID, but retain the emailExists error for a different account.

Add refresh-token hash rotation and reject sequential reuse of an old refresh token, including authentication, session domain, relational/document persistence, a fresh-install schema, and end-to-end coverage. Concurrent reuse protection and upgrading an already-deployed database require separate verification; this historical target does not establish them.
Replace separate database connection settings with one DATABASE_URL used consistently by configuration, application DB setup, Alembic, and Compose.

Use FRONTEND_HOST as the sole allowed CORS origin, retain credentials and wildcard methods/headers, and remove BACKEND_CORS_ORIGINS and its parser from application settings, Compose, and deployment documentation.

Add UTC created_at timestamps for new User and Item records, preserve existing records with nullable timestamps through an upgrade/downgrade migration, expose the nullable field through APIs and generated clients, and list users/items newest first while retaining item ownership filtering and pagination.

Reduce user enumeration by performing password-hash verification even for an unknown email. Return the same password-recovery response for registered and unknown emails while mailing only registered users, and return the invalid-token error when a reset token references an absent user. Add regression coverage; this does not guarantee identical end-to-end response timing.

Return 404 User not found when an authorized superuser reads a nonexistent user ID, preserving the existing 403 response for unauthorized ordinary users and successful reads of existing users, with regression coverage.

Add DELETE /users/me for ordinary users, delete their owned items and account together, prohibit superuser self-deletion, and restrict deletion by arbitrary user ID to superusers with a 403 permission response. Retain 404 for missing targets and add regression coverage.
